title: The Battle of Tours
description: October 732. Charles Martel's Frankish infantry must hold the wooded high ground between Tours and Poitiers against the Umayyad cavalry of Abd al-Rahman. A third force of Aquitanian allies under Duke Odo can be rallied to strike the enemy camp. Victory requires repelling the cavalry charges and forcing the invaders' withdrawal.

issues_found: All three players are assigned RANDOM civilization, so Frankish, Umayyad and Aquitanian architecture, unit skins and bonuses are left to chance — avoidable, since the engine ships Franks, Saracens/Berbers and could differentiate the Aquitanians

Player 2's strike arm includes 4 CAMEL_RIDER against only 3 SCOUT_CAVALRY: the Umayyad host at Tours was a horse-cavalry army, and the engine offers ample light/heavy horse alternatives, so the camels are an avoidable misrepresentation

Frankish force is only 5 MAN_AT_ARMS + 6 SPEARMAN + 6 ARCHER — an extremely thin 'shield-wall' for a battle whose defining feature was a deep, immovable infantry mass; archers were also a marginal element of Martel's army
Wave 3 'Third Charge' fires only a DISPLAY_INSTRUCTIONS with no PATROL actions, so the narrated third charge never actually occurs on the map

Leaders are represented by the generic KING unit (renamed), which is a non-combat, easily-killed piece; victory hinging on killing a KING makes Abd al-Rahman trivially fragile rather than a figure who fell in the melee
No explicit elevation or terrain data supporting the 'wooded high ground'; the woods are conveyed almost entirely by 4,720 oak trees

All three players are set to RANDOM civilization, so Frankish, Umayyad, and Aquitanian architecture and unit bonuses are left to chance; the engine offers Franks and Saracens/Berbers explicitly, so this is avoidable.

The Umayyad strike force is built around CAMEL_RIDER x4 as its shock arm; the army at Tours fought as Arab and Berber horse cavalry, and the engine offers knights, light cavalry and cavalry archers as better fits.
Umayyad SPEARMAN x4 in the raiding host is an odd inclusion for a force the narration explicitly characterises as all-cavalry.

Heroes are represented by KING units, which are unarmed and non-combatant; a renamed generic unit is acceptable in principle, but a KING cannot 'fall in the melee' in any meaningful way and makes the victory condition trivially achievable once reached.
'Wave 3: Third Charge' fires narration only with no PATROL or unit actions, so the third charge described in the text never actually happens on the map.

Force scale is very small (17 Frankish combatants versus 15 Umayyads) for an engagement described as a host raiding deep into Francia; the Frankish player also holds a full Town Center, Monastery, Blacksmith and production buildings, which reads as a settlement rather than a field position on wooded high ground.
